contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #060: The Global Spherical Shell conjecture.

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 060 (The Global Spherical Shell conjecture.; papers: Global Spherical Shells on Minimal Surfaces of Class VII; Lean status: UNFORMALIZED (No Lean proof in openai/math)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

Manuscript cylinder:estimate: there exist geometry-only R0,C0>0 such that every nonconstant proper holomorphic map f:Omega->Y from a cylinder domain and every measurable w>=0 with M=sup_j ||w||_{L2(Omega cap S_j)}<infinity satisfy integral_{(h f)^-1(I)} |df(partial_t)| w <= C0 M (1+E_I), for every unit interval I and finite enlarged-slab energy E_I; the same holds on a full end cut from a proper normalization.

Explicit graph filling: a locally closed holomorphic graph in D(0,2R) x B(0,4r), passing through (0,0), with vertical energy at most r^2/65536, fills D(0,R) and has image in B(0,r/2). Properness supplies local graph closedness even when source points are initially missing.

Uniform target-slab theorem with explicit constants for proper holomorphic maps from arbitrary cylinder domains into Hermitian complex surfaces with uniform centered holomorphic charts and a uniformly Lipschitz height: a fixed enlarged-slab energy E bounds integral u*w by C*M*E on the full cylinder, and by C_half*M*(1+E) on an end. Constants do not depend on map, domain, multiplier, interval length, or flat-chain length. No analytic-cycle compactness theorem or divisor-compactness premise is assumed.

Conditional compactness bridge: given the manuscripts common area exponent A, planar-normalization statement, section with end limits (1,0) and connection decay gamma>2A+10, scalar residue obstruction, and finite-dimensional fixed-bundle residue cohomology, the uniform cylinder theorem and periodic gauge produce all required current mass bounds with the same exponent A and exclude every noncompact normalization. This does not independently establish those manuscript input statements or the Global Spherical Shell conjecture.

Explicit graph filling: let D be open in the planar disk D(0,2R), G:D->B_C2(0,4r) holomorphic, and its graph closed in the entire product D(0,2R) x B_C2(0,4r). If 0 belongs to D, G(0)=0, and integral_D |G_prime|^2 <= r^2/65536, then D(0,R) is contained in D and |G|<r/2 there. Proper maps into the manuscript target supply exactly this closed-graph condition in centered charts.

If a holomorphic map G from a planar source has a relatively compact no-source-boundary component over B_C2(q,s) containing a point mapping to q, its Euclidean vertical energy on that component is at least pi*s^2. The proof uses positive orientation, Delta|G-q|^2=4|G_prime|^2, the complex Lagrange sum-of-squares identity, and Stokes on regular sublevels; holes and branching are permitted.

For all finite or one-sided infinite maximal flat-strip chains, Cauchy and zero-constant-mode Fourier estimates imply sum_j sup_Sj |df(partial_t)| <= 8*P*K*r for every integer P>=4*K^2; a doubly infinite chain forces the map to be constant. The bound is independent of chain length and target chart changes.

For every a in L1 intersect L2 on the full cylinder, a periodic solution of one-half(partial_t+i partial_theta)g=a has uniformly bounded full W12 norms on unit strips and uniformly finite integrals of exp(p*|Re g|) for every fixed finite p. The zero angular mode is retained explicitly. A direct extension/Fourier/moment proof supplies the full-norm exponential embedding, without assuming Trudinger.
Manuscript thm:main: every connected compact minimal complex surface X with b1=1, b2>0, and Kodaira dimension minus infinity contains a global spherical shell with connected complement.

Manuscript curve:area: the divisor of any bounded negative-end holomorphic section of a compact datum has unit-negative-height-slab area at most C*exp(A*l), where A>0 depends only on lifted coordinate geometry, not on decay rate; the same A applies to reduced components and every fixed deck translate.

Manuscript curve:genus: every divisor-component normalization has no nonzero L2 scalar holomorphic differential, has genus zero, and if noncompact is biholomorphic to a domain in the Riemann sphere with arbitrary connectivity.

Manuscript compact:section and curve:gamma-choice: for each required compact datum there exists a holomorphic bundle E and a nonzero section s with prescribed end limits (1,0), divisor D bounded above in height, and connection error decaying at any prescribed finite rate gamma, chosen greater than 2A+10 after fixing the geometry-only area exponent A.

Manuscript weighted:currents: for fixed rates (-eps,b) with b>eps>0 the stepped (2,q) current complex has finite-dimensional cohomology for E, zero degree-one scalar cohomology, and every (2,0)-primitive of a bounded-above-supported (2,1) current vanishes on a positive tail. An order-zero current with negative-slab mass exponent mu<b belongs to degree one W^-4 in that same fixed complex.

Manuscript curve:residue: nonzero holomorphic normalization differentials on distinct bounded-above closed irreducible curves, with coefficient bundle F fixed and all mass exponents below fixed b, give linearly independent classes in the same weighted degree-one cohomology. For the scalar bundle even one such differential is impossible.
Manuscript cylinder:compactness: every irreducible component of the constructed divisor D is compact and has rational normalization.

Manuscript conclusion:curves and conclusion:upper-bound: the compact-datum pairing and compact rational divisor components imply at least b2(X) rational curves on X, while the no-square-zero case has at most b2(X) curves; the shell criterion then applies.

Manuscript surface:reduction: a minimal class VII surface with b2>0 has a global spherical shell if it has a nonzero square-zero effective divisor or exactly b2 rational curves. These are external surface-theoretic inputs, not verified in the cylinder mission.

Conditional compactness bridge: given the manuscripts common area exponent A, planar-normalization statement, section with end limits (1,0) and connection decay gamma>2A+10, scalar residue obstruction, and finite-dimensional fixed-bundle residue cohomology, the uniform cylinder theorem and periodic gauge produce all required current mass bounds with the same exponent A and exclude every noncompact normalization. This does not independently establish those manuscript input statements or the Global Spherical Shell conjecture.

claims.natural_statement: Manuscript compact:classes: for every n there are d>=n*b2(X)-C0 compact line-bundle classes supported in one open period, with independent transferred classes modulo torsion, e_i^2=K_Y.e_i=-m_i<0 for positive integers m_i, and matching compact and transferred pairings. This is an open upstream construction, not verified by the cylinder theorem.

routes.retired_because: Primary texts of Harvey-Shiffman Theorems 3.9-3.10 and Bishop could not be obtained through the bounded legal access routes tried. Search summaries are not accepted as theorem evidence. The replacement route proves graph filling directly by Stokes and the holomorphic area lower bound.

This preliminary decomposition listed graph filling alone. A full universal estimate also needs an independent flat-chain summability obligation, now recorded in R_CYL_FULL_CHARGING. Graph filling alone was never a complete proof of the slab theorem.
